note: The wording that tools/bench/rubric_eval.py evaluated as prompt variant clartb (tie-breaks from the annotation rubric tests/classifier_synthetic_v2/rubric.md; clarifications written after reading DEV failures only), kept as data so the server prompt equals the evaluated one. No clinical requirement is stated.
tie_breaks: Tie-breaks (from the annotation rubric): asking the patient for name, date of birth or wristband is CONFIRM_IDENTITY; asking about or stating an allergy to the patient is STATE_ALLERGY, never ASK_TOPIC; asking for agreement to the operation or a signature is CONSENT_SIGN. To a colleague, stating an allergy, a not-fasted state, an identity mismatch or a worsening sign is HANDOVER_CRITICAL_ELEMENT. Asking a colleague to do a task (test, medicine, transport, call) is VOICE_ORDER; asking a senior to come, advise or decide is ESCALATE_SPEECH. Repeating an instruction or result back to the colleague who gave it is CLOSED_LOOP; noting back what the patient said is ACKNOWLEDGE_FACT. Explaining the operation is EXPLAIN_PROCEDURE, a test or monitor EXPLAIN_TEST, what you are about to do to the patient now EXPLAIN_ACTION. Giving the patient information that fits nothing else is ANSWER_QUESTION. Asking to repeat or explain something unclear is CLARIFY; asking the patient to say back what they understood is CHECK_UNDERSTANDING.
clarifications: Clarifications (written after reading DEV failures only): intended means the SPEAKER says they will do the act themselves later ("I'll ask about that in a moment"). Telling the patient what will happen, how long it takes or what the operation involves is the act of explaining or answering, performed now: it is SUPPORTED, not intended and not hypothetical. A statement the speaker makes to the patient about what is true is not reported speech. If words are cut off or mis-heard but the act can still be recognised, judge the act the words most likely carry; use UNCERTAIN only when it cannot be recovered. Report an objective that is SUPPORTED once only.
